summary_en: Dividend per share for the fiscal year ending November 2026 raised to 75 yen from prior guidance of 72 yen, with period-end dividend increased to 39 yen from 36 yen. DOE expected to reach 4.7%, above the 4.0% policy benchmark. Payout ratio to exceed 50% threshold.
title_en: Notice of Revision of Dividend Forecast for Fiscal Year Ended November 2026 (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Moriotstock announced on November 19, 2026 that it has revised its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending November 2026 at a board meeting held that day. The annual dividend per share has been raised to 75 yen from the previous guidance of 72 yen issued on January 14, 2026, representing a 3-yen increase. The period-end dividend was increased to 39 yen from the previously forecast 36 yen. The mid-term dividend remains at 36 yen as already paid.

The company bases its dividend policy on three key principles: (1) stable and continuous dividend payment, (2) a consolidated dividend on equity (DOE) benchmark of 4.0%, and (3) a payout ratio of 50% or higher relative to net income attributable to parent company shareholders depending on business performance. Under the revised forecast, DOE is expected to reach 4.7%, exceeding the 4.0% policy benchmark, while the payout ratio is projected to exceed the 50% threshold.

The company also disclosed that it will revise its dividend policy framework as announced on July 14, 2026, effective from the fiscal year ending November 2027. The revised policy raises the DOE benchmark to 5.0% and targets a 6.0% DOE by the final year of the 9th medium-term business plan in fiscal 2031. The new policy maintains the 50% minimum payout ratio and introduces an emphasis on progressive dividend growth. These revisions are designed to align shareholder returns with the medium-term plan targets, reinforcing management focus on capital efficiency and revenue growth.
